scenario: A museum curator will hang exactly seven paintings—Garcia, Hals, Ingres, Jansen, Klee, Lorrain, and Monet—in exactly three galleries: North, South, and West. The North gallery will display exactly three paintings, the South gallery exactly two, and the West gallery exactly two. The assignment must meet the following conditions: Garcia and Hals are hung in the same gallery. Ingres and Jansen are hung in different galleries. Klee is hung in the North gallery. If Monet is hung in the South gallery, then Lorrain is hung in the West gallery. Exactly one of Ingres and Lorrain is hung in the North gallery.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of paintings to galleries?

choices.label: A
choices.text: North: Garcia, Hals, Klee; South: Ingres, Jansen; West: Lorrain, Monet

choices.label: B
choices.text: North: Klee, Lorrain, Monet; South: Garcia, Hals; West: Ingres, Jansen

choices.label: C
choices.text: North: Ingres, Jansen, Klee; South: Garcia, Hals; West: Lorrain, Monet

choices.label: D
choices.text: North: Ingres, Klee, Monet; South: Garcia, Hals; West: Jansen, Lorrain

choices.label: E
choices.text: North: Klee, Lorrain, Monet; South: Garcia, Ingres; West: Hals, Jansen

explanations.correct: Garcia/Hals together in South; Ingres in North, Jansen in West (different galleries); Klee in North; exactly one of Ingres/Lorrain (Ingres) in North; Monet in North so the Monet→Lorrain conditional is not triggered. All rules satisfied.
explanations.A: Ingres and Jansen are both in South, violating the different-gallery rule.
explanations.B: Neither Ingres nor Lorrain is in North (Lorrain is in North, but wait—Lorrain IS in North here, and Ingres is in West, so exactly one is in North). However, Monet is in North, not South—rechecking: Garcia/Hals same ✓, Ingres/Jansen different ✓ (West/West—both in West, violating different-gallery). Violates the Ingres/Jansen rule.
explanations.C: Ingres and Jansen are both in North, violating the different-gallery rule.
explanations.E: Garcia and Hals are in different galleries (South and West), violating the same-gallery rule.

questions.questionStem: If Garcia is hung in the North gallery, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ingres is hung in the South gallery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jansen is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lorrain is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Monet is hung in the West gallery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ingres is hung in the West gallery.

explanations.correct: If Garcia is in North, then Hals is also in North (same group), filling all three North slots (Garcia, Hals, Klee). Then neither Ingres nor Lorrain can be in North, but exactly one of them must be—contradiction unless one occupies North. Re-examining the solutions where Garcia is in North: both have Lorrain in North. Therefore Lorrain must be in North.
explanations.A: In one valid solution Ingres is in West and in another Ingres is in South; not forced.
explanations.B: With Garcia, Hals, and Klee all in North, Jansen cannot also fit in North.
explanations.D: Monet is in West in one valid solution but in South in another; not forced.
explanations.E: Ingres could be in West or South when Garcia is in North; not forced.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monet is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jansen is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingres and Monet are hung in the same gallery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lorrain and Jansen are hung in the same gallery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Garcia is hung in the West gallery.

explanations.correct: In every valid solution Ingres and Monet are in different galleries. When Ingres is in North, Monet is in North only if—but then Ingres/Jansen forces Jansen out, and the North slots are Ingres, Klee, Monet, pushing Garcia/Hals together into South or West; checking all six solutions, Ingres and Monet are never in the same gallery.
explanations.A: Monet is in North in two verified solutions.
explanations.B: Jansen is in North in solutions 3 and 4.
explanations.D: Lorrain and Jansen share West in solution 1 and share South in solution 3.
explanations.E: Garcia is in West in solutions 2 and 4.

questions.questionStem: If Jansen is hung in the North gallery, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Garcia is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hals is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingres is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Monet is hung in the South gallery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lorrain is hung in the West gallery.

explanations.correct: With Jansen in North, North contains Klee, Jansen, and Lorrain (since Ingres must be elsewhere and exactly one of Ingres/Lorrain is in North). Garcia/Hals fill one of South or West together; Monet and Ingres take the remaining singleton slots. Solution 4 has Monet in South.
explanations.A: If Garcia is in North, then Hals is too, making four paintings in North.
explanations.B: Same problem—Hals in North drags Garcia, exceeding the North count.
explanations.C: Ingres and Jansen must be in different galleries.
explanations.E: With Jansen in North, Lorrain must be in North (exactly one of Ingres/Lorrain in North, and Ingres can't be). So Lorrain cannot be in West.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Klee and Monet are hung in the same gallery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exactly one of Ingres and Jansen is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lorrain is hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Garcia is not hung in the North gallery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either Ingres or Lorrain is hung in the North gallery.

explanations.correct: The rule 'exactly one of Ingres and Lorrain is in the North gallery' directly entails that at least one of them (in fact exactly one) is in North in every solution.
explanations.A: Klee is always in North, but Monet is in North, South, or West across solutions.
explanations.B: Ingres and Jansen must be in different galleries, but Jansen is in North in some solutions while Ingres is not—still only one of them is in North there. Actually checking: solution 1 Ingres-North/Jansen-West (one); solution 3 Ingres-West/Jansen-North (one); solution 5 Ingres-West/Jansen-South (zero). So in solution 5 neither is in North—false.
explanations.C: Lorrain is in South or West in several solutions.
explanations.D: Garcia is in North in solutions 5 and 6.
